thread:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a microprofile speculative calibration on draft-ozma-13b-q4 today, notes below
jon: nice, did you use the new micro-bench harness or the old runner?
maya: bench-v2 (lightweight microprofile). per-token latency histograms + outlier tracing. warmup=20, batch=1, seq=512
sasha: what quality metrics did you track?
maya: ppl on heldout, EM on trivia100, and BERTScore on a 200-example summarization subset. also manual spot-checks for hallucinations
leo: numbers?
maya: mean token latency dropped ~1.35x (22ms -> 16.3ms). 99th went from ~80ms -> ~46ms with speculative prefetch path
anita: sweet, any regressions?
maya: small quality deltas in quantized q4 path: BERTScore -0.8 pts on summarization, trivia EM -0.4%. most regressions concentrated on long-context summaries (>400 tokens)
jon: can you paste the exact command you ran?
maya: ```
./bench.py --model draft-ozma-13b-q4 --decode speculative --microprofile --warmup 20 --seq 512 --batch 1 --kv_prefetch 0.6 --seeds 3 --out results/microprof-1766543210.json\```
infra-bot: deploy job queued: infra/job/bench/1766543210 status: SUCCESS (artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/microprof-1766543210.json)
sasha: did you try disabling kv prefetch or lowering the heuristic? curious about mispredict vs extra work trade-off
maya: yes — ran a sweep kv_prefetch=[0.0,0.3,0.6,0.9]. 0.0 has fewer speculative mistakes but worse latency; 0.6 hit best sweet spot for 99th reduction with minimal EM regressions
leo: how did you detect hallucination spikes? any automated rule?
maya: logged token-level surprisal + semantic drift score; example anomaly: "prompt#1245: hallucination spike at token 412" flagged by drift>0.35 + repetition heuristics
jon: for canary rollout, recommend: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% with automated EM/BERTScore guard rails and immediate rollback on >1% EM drop for trivia holdouts
anita: add prompt-sensitive holdouts: long-context summarization + codegen small set (50 examples)
ops-bot: created ticket INF-4521: canary config + eval hooks (assignee: maya)
maya: next steps I propose: (1) expand holdout set to 2k prompts covering long-context, codegen, and instruction-following; (2) run seeds x3 for stability; (3) throughput test on 8xA100 dedicated nodes to validate real latency under load; (4) add regression alert thresholds to eval board
sasha: please post CSVs and raw logs to the eval board and link PR. Also include per-prompt deltas so we can triage outliers
maya: will open PR with summary + raw artifacts. quick sample of per-prompt CSV header: "prompt_id,metric,baseline,speculative,delta,notes"
jon: nice. also consider adding a tiny grammar-check eval for summarization to catch phrasing regressions
leo: can we run a fast shadow for 24 hours at 2% traffic before canary? gets more real-world diversity
anita: +1 for shadow run and add checks for repetition rate and token-level entropy
maya: agreed — scheduling shadow 24h @2% before 5% canary. will attach the run plan to INF-4521
jon: thanks maya — this looks actionable. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://bench-artifacts/microprof-1766543210.json, s3://logs/microprof-1766543210-traces.tar.gz
maya: tagging results in eval board and will ping when PR is up. sync tomorrow 10:00 PT for a 15m triage?
leo: yep, on my calendar.
anita: I'll join too.
ops-bot: calendar invite created: "Speculative microprofile calibration sync" tomorrow 10:00 PT (guests: maya, jon, sasha, leo, anita)
